_about: Facts shown in the showcase. Every figure is copied from a recorded project file named in 'source'. Edit here, not in the JavaScript.

project.title: Document Classifier
project.subtitle: Capstone · Inventory Management System
project.one_liner: Reads a photo of a printed business document and sorts it into one of four types, then shows why.

classes.name: Purchase order
classes.what: A buyer asks a supplier for goods.
classes.cue: "Purchase Order" heading, or Order No + Required By + Please supply

classes.name: Receipt
classes.what: Proof that a sale was paid.
classes.cue: Usually decided by the learned model from words like totals, cash, change

classes.name: Delivery note
classes.what: Goods sent or delivered (challan, packing slip).

classes.name: Customer copy
classes.what: A copy-marked document (Customer / Office copy, Duplicate).
classes.cue: Copy marker, tolerant to one OCR mistake ("uplicate")

pipeline.detail: Phone photo or scan of a printed page (JPEG, PNG, HEIC…)
Lighting correction, then Tesseract reads the text from several page views
Looks for explicit headings, copy markers and purchase-request fields
If no rule decides: TF-IDF word features + Complement Naive Bayes
One of four types, with the exact text or word weights behind it

headline.label: Runs on this laptop
headline.note: No cloud, API key or GPU

journey.name: Image-only baseline
journey.note: Looked at pixels only. Confused delivery notes with purchase orders.

journey.name: Text classifier
journey.note: Reading the text beat looking at the image. Delivery notes still weak (1/10).

journey.name: Printed-only + headings
journey.method: Same text model + printed heading and page-edge rules
journey.note: Scope narrowed to printed documents. New grouped validation split created.

journey.name: MiniLM transformer
journey.method: Frozen MiniLM sentence encoder + logistic head + rules
journey.note: One more document right, but needs downloaded transformer weights.

journey.name: Explainable hybrid
journey.method: Lighting-corrected OCR + printed rules + Complement NB
journey.note: Best result, fully explainable, no transformer weights needed.

journey_sets.old_test: Historical 28-document test set, older scope that still included handwriting

rejected.name: Small BERT fine-tuning
rejected.why: Memorised training (143/150) but did not generalise

rejected.name: BERT + word feature fusion
rejected.why: No better than the simpler model

rejected.name: Contrastive MiniLM adaptation
rejected.why: 40 training steps did not help on this data size

rejected.name: Extra sparse OCR passes
rejected.why: More OCR text added noise, not signal

rejected.name: Fine-tuning image model
rejected.why: Document type lives in the words, not the layout

sources.name: Our phone photos of printed synthetic documents

gaps.title: No independent real-document test yet
gaps.detail: 92% is measured on a validation set we also used while improving the rules. A fresh holdout of real documents has a written plan (80 documents, 20 per type) but 0 collected.

gaps.title: Customer copies are thin
gaps.detail: Only 8 customer copies in training. Both validation mistakes are customer copies with faint or red stamps.

gaps.title: Validation delivery notes are synthetic
gaps.detail: All 3 validation delivery notes are photos of our printed synthetic documents.

gaps.title: Labels not human-verified
gaps.detail: Labels and transcriptions were reviewed by AI and the team, but none are formally human-verified yet.

gaps.title: Printed documents only
gaps.detail: Handwriting is out of scope by decision on 20 Oct. Signatures are ignored.

decisions.question: What should the next two to three weeks focus on?
decisions.why: The classifier works on development data. The next step decides what the final report can claim.

options.title: Prove it on real documents
options.detail: Collect 80 new real documents (20 per type) from new shops and suppliers, then test once. Gives an honest accuracy number for the report.

options.title: Fix the weak class
options.detail: Gather more customer-copy layouts and improve reading of faint or red stamps.

options.title: Move on to extraction
options.detail: Pull items, quantities and totals out of each document. A local prototype already exists (port 8772).

options.title: Build the end-to-end app
options.detail: Phone capture → classifier → stored record in a simple inventory screen.

decisions.question: What result should count as "done" for the classifier?
decisions.why: Sets the bar for the report and tells us when to stop tuning.

options.title: 90% or more on real holdout
options.detail: Matches the current development figure. May need more data to reach.

options.title: 85% or more on real holdout
options.detail: Realistic for a first independent test of a small-data model.

options.title: Report current result with limits
options.detail: Use 23/25 development validation and clearly state it is not independent.

decisions.question: A purchase order or delivery note stamped "Customer Copy": which label wins?
decisions.why: Still an open taxonomy decision. It changes how real documents are labelled.

options.title: Copy wins
options.detail: Any copy marker means customer_copy (current behaviour).

options.title: Document type wins
options.detail: Label by what the document is; ignore the copy stamp.

options.title: Type plus a separate copy flag
options.detail: Predict the type and an is_copy yes/no. Needs a small model change.

decisions.question: Should handwriting stay out of scope?
decisions.why: Printed-only was chosen on 20 Oct to make the problem solvable in time.

options.title: Add handwritten fields later
options.detail: Printed forms with handwritten values, after the holdout.

options.title: Include handwriting now
options.detail: Needs new data and a different OCR approach.
